symbols.name: source length
symbols.meaning: The number of coordinates of the source vector, which is the length of the source transform.
symbols.quote: Take coprime integers $s<t$, where $s$ is the number of coordinates of the source vector and $t$ the number of coordinates of the target.

symbols.name: target length
symbols.meaning: The number of coordinates of the target vector, which is the length of the target transform.
symbols.quote: Take coprime integers $s<t$, where $s$ is the number of coordinates of the source vector and $t$ the number of coordinates of the target.

symbols.name: source transform
symbols.meaning: The normalized Fourier transform of length $s$.
symbols.quote: $F_s$ is the normalized transform of length $s$, and $F_t$ is the one of length $t$.

symbols.name: target transform
symbols.meaning: The normalized Fourier transform of length $t$.
symbols.quote: $F_s$ is the normalized transform of length $s$, and $F_t$ is the one of length $t$.

symbols.name: source permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation on length-$s$ vectors that sends $u$ to the vector with entries $u_{tj}$.
symbols.quote: $P_s$ is the coordinate permutation $(P_s u)_j = u_{tj}$, with indices taken modulo $s$.

symbols.name: target permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation on length-$t$ vectors that sends $v$ to the vector with entries $v_{-sk}$.
symbols.quote: $P_t$ is the coordinate permutation $(P_t v)_k = v_{-sk}$, with indices taken modulo $t$.

symbols.name: length excess
symbols.meaning: The relative excess $t/s-1$ of the target length over the source length.
symbols.quote: Let $\theta = t/s-1$ be the relative excess of $t$ over $s$.

symbols.name: Gaussian width
symbols.meaning: The integer width of the Gaussians used in the maps, with $\alpha \ge 2$.
symbols.quote: The identity needs $\theta > p/\alpha^4$, where $\alpha \ge 2$ is an integer Gaussian width and $p$ is the integer precision of the numerical approximation.

symbols.name: precision
symbols.meaning: The integer precision of the numerical approximation.
symbols.quote: The identity needs $\theta > p/\alpha^4$, where $\alpha \ge 2$ is an integer Gaussian width and $p$ is the integer precision of the numerical approximation.

symbols.name: source-to-target Gaussian map
symbols.meaning: The Gaussian map from length-$s$ vectors to length-$t$ vectors defined by $(Su)_k=\frac{1}{\alpha}\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}} e^{-\pi\alpha^{-2}(j-sk/t)^2}u_j$.
symbols.quote: $S$ maps length-$s$ vectors to length-$t$ vectors by $(Su)_k=\frac{1}{\alpha}\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}} e^{-\pi\alpha^{-2}(j-sk/t)^2}u_j$.

symbols.name: second Gaussian map
symbols.meaning: The Gaussian map from length-$s$ vectors to length-$t$ vectors defined by $(Tu)_k=\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}} e^{-\pi\alpha^{2}(tj/s-k)^2}u_j$.
symbols.quote: $T$ maps length-$s$ vectors to length-$t$ vectors by $(Tu)_k=\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}} e^{-\pi\alpha^{2}(tj/s-k)^2}u_j$.

symbols.name: selection map
symbols.meaning: The map from length-$t$ vectors to length-$s$ vectors that picks out, for each $j$, the entry at the integer nearest to $tj/s$.
symbols.quote: $C$ selects, for each $j<s$, the entry of a length-$t$ vector at the integer nearest to $tj/s$.

symbols.name: diagonal correction
symbols.meaning: The diagonal map on length-$s$ vectors that multiplies entry $j$ by the reciprocal of the Gaussian factor at the entry that $C$ selects.
symbols.quote: $D$ is the diagonal map that multiplies entry $j$ by the reciprocal of the Gaussian factor at that selected entry.

symbols.name: correction map
symbols.meaning: The map $CTD$ on length-$s$ vectors, which is close to the identity.
symbols.quote: Put $N = CTD$, the correction map on length-$s$ vectors.

symbols.name: source contraction
symbols.meaning: The contraction $S/2$ from length-$s$ vectors to length-$t$ vectors.

symbols.name: target contraction
symbols.meaning: The contraction $2^{-(2\alpha^2-2)}DN^{-1}C/2$ from length-$t$ vectors to length-$s$ vectors.

relations.quote: Gaussian resampling is an identity that replaces the [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) of an arbitrary length by transforms whose lengths are powers of two.
Gaussian resampling serves the [Radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md) of two integers' digit vectors, since that convolution uses such transforms.
